dense.reuse: existing ordinary weak reuse plus dense factor pages

direct.reuse: strong adaptive direct map; ordinary and factor reuse bypassed

budgetRationale: Identical 512 MiB query budgets preserve the unrefused dense fixture configuration. Heap and global ledger remain 1 GiB. Array-only direct memo accounting is not a complete retained-memory bound.

directMemoAccountingPolicy.adaptiveOutcomes: Low-hit disabling, varying collisions, growth, and replacement are measured outcomes; they never select or discard queries.
directMemoAccountingPolicy.export: Thirteen primitive records are preallocated before the unchanged launcher; serialize after its return.
directMemoAccountingPolicy.mapping: Ordinary and dense create no direct-memo owner; direct creates 13. Direct owner and semantic-compile ordinals are 1..13; lazy-value interval differences exactly match original raw query counters without inter-owner gaps.
directMemoAccountingPolicy.naturalCollection: No explicit GC, profiler, heap walk, weak-miss exclusion, or replacement query.
directMemoAccountingPolicy.observerLimit: No new per-target/factor-page or weak-miss observer; original coordinate-owner admission counters remain available. Dense factor-page refusal is not separately counted by this new helper.
directMemoAccountingPolicy.resolverPolicy: Raw resolver differences are outcomes, not rejection criteria. No count tolerance, residual gate, causal subtraction, or timing/allocation normalization.

directMemoPolicy.accountingLimit: Array storage only. Retained Values, lexical data, revision/owner graphs, and later lazy initialization are not bounded by this charge.
directMemoPolicy.admissionFailure: Permanently disable and resolve normally; no weak-cache fallback in direct mode.
directMemoPolicy.arrays: ID long[], semantic-version long[], full-mask int[], strong Value[], and InternalIdentity[]; the fifth array strengthens the four-array sketch against revision/identity changes without a semantic-version bump.
directMemoPolicy.collision: An occupied bucket with a different full key; replacement on admission, no LRU.
directMemoPolicy.counters: Cumulative per native iteration; scope clears do not restart the adaptive policy.
directMemoPolicy.firstBoundary: After probe 8192, permanently disable when cumulative hits are below 25 percent; no growth at this boundary.
directMemoPolicy.growth: Rehash in deterministic old-slot order and discard colliding entries; reserve complete replacement arrays while the old arrays remain live.
directMemoPolicy.hitMeaning: Hits count validated table candidates. Standalone access may still resolve such a candidate to preserve source ownership handoff; outward capture passes its actual Sail exposure token. Raw resolver counts remain authoritative.
directMemoPolicy.publication: Publish an admitted miss immediately, before the next projected value is resolved.
directMemoPolicy.stability: Exact source identity, non-null stable result-view and exposure scopes, semantic version, and the captured ID/revision-number/revision-owner witness.
directMemoPolicy.subsequentBoundaries: At 16384 and each subsequent multiple of 8192, double up to 65536 when cumulative hits are at least 25 percent and cumulative collisions at least 12.5 percent.

estimand: Total query-cost effect of replacing existing result reuse with the adaptive strong direct map, including transport, strong retention, adaptation, allocation, natural GC, and resolver changes.
failurePolicy: Stop and preserve all outputs on process, result, route, source, lifecycle, counter-consistency, unexpected mutation/unsupported-value, or admission failure. Raw resolver differences and low-hit disabling remain valid outcomes. No replacement, exclusions, favorable tails, extra rounds, or forced routes.

fanout.oracle: Independent full-bag row count and lexical checksum; original consumption unchanged.

shared-tail.oracle: Exact independent IRI types, lexical values, tuple/parent association, legal unique dense row keys, complete count/checksum.

name: Adaptive strong direct-memo total effect under natural GC
observerLimitations: Adaptive counters are intrinsic to the direct algorithm. Primitive lifecycle exports occur at owner open/close and JSON only after the launcher returns. Ordinary/dense create no direct owner. Costs of helper branches/lifecycle observation are included; no uninstrumented counterfactual is estimated.
perFixtureStoreConfiguration: Fanout retains AUTO direct-adjacency max bytes; shared-tail retains explicit 1 GiB direct-adjacency budget. Every arm within a fixture matches.
pooling: No pooling with historical baselines, Stage 2, incomplete publication comparison, compact-page, frame-guard, shared-tail pilot, or diagnostics.
quietPeriod: One serial Java process; no simultaneous builds, tests, profiles, compression, or heavy hashing during timing.
resultGate: Independent expected counts/checksums, exact shared-tail bag oracle, ledger endpoints zero, valid all-thread allocation, prescribed direct owner count and query mapping, consistent table statistics, and matched routes/tiers/adjacency.

statistics.policy: Two separately evaluated engineering screens: direct/ordinary and direct/dense. Dense/ordinary is descriptive. No significance or production-promotion claim.
statistics.preparation: Warm preparation and first cold query separately. Cold query starts after fixture construction and excludes JVM launch. Preserve all eight warmups.
statistics.primary: Each fresh JVM contributes the median of all five measurements. Ratios pair the same fixture and round. Report median and full range of six ratios. Never pool fixtures.

strategy: Normal AUTO; no forced strategy or tier. Every measured query must use compiled native IR and the same route histogram within its fixture.

totalEffectScreen.interpretation: Apply the engineering screen separately against ordinary and dense; descriptive results always reported. Neither significance nor production promotion.
totalEffectScreen.rationale: A 5 percent median reduction on both fixtures with all six paired reductions is a useful engineering effect; allocation is separately screened. Value payload retention remains unbounded by the array ledger.
